note: §17.557 — goldens for `model_ab.py --task extraction`. Each item feeds gt_extractor's DISTILL_SYSTEM/DISTILL_PROMPT + RECORD_DISTILLED_ENTRIES_TOOL (the production distill path). Scoring is reliability, not correctness: did the model emit a parseable non-empty `entries` tool-call (native or coaxed). Use it to A/B a role/model change before shipping it (cf. §17.556 — coaxed qwen3.5 5/5 vs native kimi 1/5 on this prompt). §17.992 — goldens may set `expect: "empty"`, meaning a corpus with nothing on-topic where REFUSING is the correct answer; a model that pads off-topic entries fails those.

results.title: 8086 Memory Segmentation Explained
results.content: The 8086 uses a segmented memory model. A 20-bit physical address is formed by shifting the 16-bit segment register left 4 bits and adding the 16-bit offset, yielding a 1 MB address space from 16-bit registers.

results.title: DOS INT 21h Services
results.content: INT 21h is the primary DOS API interrupt. AH selects the function: 01h read char, 02h write char, 09h print string, 4Ch terminate. Parameters pass in registers.

results.title: BIOS Keyboard Interrupt 16h
results.content: INT 16h provides BIOS keyboard services. AH=00h waits for and reads a keystroke (scan code in AH, ASCII in AL); AH=01h checks status without blocking.

results.title: Real Mode vs Protected Mode
results.content: Real mode uses segment:offset addressing with a 1 MB limit. Protected mode (80286+) adds descriptor tables, privilege levels, and access to extended memory beyond 1 MB.

results.title: Hybrid retrieval: dense + sparse fusion
results.content: Hybrid search combines a dense vector leg (semantic embeddings) with a sparse leg (BM25 lexical scoring) and fuses the two rank lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), which is robust to differing score scales.

results.title: Reranking with cross-encoders
results.content: A cross-encoder reranker jointly encodes the query and each candidate document, producing a relevance score. It is more accurate than bi-encoder retrieval but quadratically more expensive, so it is applied only to the top-k candidates.

results.title: Chunking strategies for RAG
results.content: Document chunking trades recall against precision: small chunks improve precision but fragment context; overlap between chunks preserves cross-boundary context at the cost of redundancy.

results.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: Logical Replication
results.content: Logical replication was introduced in PostgreSQL 10. It replicates changes based on replication identity, usually a primary key, rather than block addresses.

results.title: Replication Slots
results.content: A replication slot retains WAL segments until consumed. An inactive slot can cause unbounded WAL growth; max_slot_wal_keep_size (PostgreSQL 13+) bounds it.

results.title: pg_replication_slots view
results.content: The pg_replication_slots view shows slot_name, plugin, slot_type (physical or logical), active, and restart_lsn for every slot.
